name: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Morea Eyalet, the Eyalet of the Archipelago and the Pashalik of Yanina, the entities the First Hellenic Republic page lists as preceding it (Cliopatria's 1822 shape: the Peloponnese and parts of…

successors.name: Kingdom of Greece
successors.text: the Greek state after the Axis occupation of 1941-1944

ledger.x: 1822: the Greek revolutionaries proclaim independence ('Proclamation of Independence: 1 January 1822') and form a central administration 'at the First National Assembly of Epidaurus in early 1822'.
1824: central Greece and the Cretan holdings drop out of the Cliopatria shape.
February 1825: Ibrahim's Egyptian army lands in the Peloponnese.
1825: the south-west Peloponnese passes to the Egyptian-Ottoman army.
1826: Missolonghi falls.
1827: the Third National Assembly at Troezen establishes the Hellenic State.
1828: the Peloponnese and central Greece are retaken.
September 1829: the fighting ends with the Russo-Turkish war.
3 February 1830: independence recognised.
1832: Greece becomes a kingdom under the Bavarian prince Otto.
21 July 1832: the Treaty of Constantinople fixes the northern frontier 'along the Arta-Volos line', the 14 cells Cliopatria adds in Aetolia-Acarnania and Phthiotis.
1834: the capital moves from Nafplio to Athens ('Nafplio (1832-1834); Athens (1834-1973)').
23 October 1862: King Otto is ousted; the Danish prince George becomes king in 1863.
21 May 1864: the Ionian Islands join Greece.
ledger.cpn: United States of the Ionian Islands

ledger.x: 2 July 1881: Thessaly and part of Epirus pass to Greece.
October 1908: Crete declares its union with Greece.
October 1912: the First Balkan War opens the Greek front in Epirus and Macedonia.
21 October 1912: Preveza is taken.
9 November 1912: Thessaloniki surrenders.
6 March 1913: Ioannina falls.
16 March 1913: Samos is Greek.
March 1913: the fighting on the Greek-Ottoman front ends with Ioannina (6 March) and Samos (16 March); the Treaty of London that ended the war is not dated on the pages opened for Greece.
June 1913: the Second Balkan War.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Second Balkan War ('concluded on 10 August 1913').
10 August 1913: Greece gets eastern Macedonia.
14 December 1913: Crete is taken over.
February 1914: the Great Powers recognise Greek sovereignty over the north-eastern Aegean islands, 'undetermined until the Great Powers recognized it in February 1914'.
1916: eastern Macedonia leaves the Greek shape.
1919: the eastern Macedonian cells return to the Cliopatria shape.
15 May 1919: Greece lands at Smyrna.
27 November 1919: the Treaty of Neuilly takes Western Thrace from Bulgaria.
Summer 1920: Greek offensives extend the zone to Bursa and Usak.
10 August 1920: the Treaty of Sevres gives Greece Eastern Thrace.
9 September 1922: Turkish forces enter Smyrna.
September 1922: the whole Anatolian zone is lost.
15 October 1922: Eastern Thrace is evacuated.
25 March 1924: the Second Hellenic Republic is proclaimed.
10 October 1935: the monarchy is restored.
1940: Cliopatria's row ends here, not the Greek state.

wars.name: Greek War of Independence
wars.outcome: Greek autonomy accepted at Adrianople (September 1829), independence recognised in the London Protocol of February 1830; the Arta-Volos frontier fixed by the Treaty of Constantinople on 21 July 1832.

wars.name: First Balkan War
wars.outcome: Greece takes Epirus south of the future Albanian frontier, southern Macedonia with Thessaloniki, Crete and the Aegean islands; confirmed by the Treaty of Bucharest of 10 August 1913.

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: Bulgaria loses; the Greek-Bulgarian border moves east to beyond Kavala; Treaty of Bucharest, 10 August 1913.

wars.name: Greco-Turkish War (1919-1922)
wars.outcome: Greek defeat at Sakarya (1921) and Dumlupinar (30 August 1922); Smyrna lost 9 September 1922; Eastern Thrace evacuated after the Armistice of Mudanya (11 October 1922).

wars.name: Greco-Italian War
wars.outcome: 'Italian troops crossed the border on 28 October 1940'; the page opened gives no territorial result.

certainty.note: A revolutionary front that moved with every campaign; no treaty line until the London Protocol of February 1830, and the Arta-Volos line only in 1832.
The Arta-Volos line of the Treaty of Constantinople (1832) and the border treaty of 24 May 1881 with the convention of 2 July 1881; the Ionian Islands transfer of 1864 is a treaty.
The Balkan War fronts move monthly; Epirus, Macedonia and the islands harden with the Treaty of Bucharest (10 August 1913).
The Bucharest frontiers; the north-eastern Aegean islands were recognised in February 1914.
Occupation and war: eastern Macedonia 1916-1918, the Smyrna zone and Anatolian advance 1919-1922, Eastern Thrace 1920-1922.
The Neuilly and Lausanne frontiers; the Lausanne date is not on the pages opened.
